newsitem.title: USA: Rockefeller Center sued over cash-out merger.
newsitem.headline: Rockefeller Center sued over cash-out merger.

text.p: Lawyers representing former stockholders of Rockefeller Center Properties Inc said on Wednesday that the former real estate investment trust is being sued for allegedly misleading shareholders about a cash-out merger.

The lawyers, Pamela Tikellis, James Malone and Michael Donovan of the Chimicles, Jacobsen & Tikellis law firm, contend a buyout group "threatened, coerced and pressured" Rockefeller Center shareholders to relinquish their shares for less than they were worth.
Rockefeller Center Properties, which held a $1.3 billion mortgage to the landmark 12-building complex in midtown Manhattan, was acquired in July by the group for $8.00 per share.
The group, which is named in the lawsuit, include David Rockefeller, Daniel Niedich, Goldman Sachs & Co and Whitehall Street Real Estate Limited Partnership V.
Also named as defendants were former Rockefeller Center Chairman Peter Linneman and former President Richard Scarlata.
The parties named in the lawsuit could not be immediately reached for comment.
Rockfeller Center Properties received the properties under a bankruptcy reorganization by the two partnerships that had owned the buildings. It had held the mortgage on the properties.
The lawyers contend the $8.00 per share price is below what they consider to be the complex's actual worth of at least $1.5 billion to $2.2 billion.

The lawsuit contends the company failed to disclose there would be "more than sufficient cash resources or financings available...to secure and maintain ownership of Rockefeller Center," according to a statement issued by the lawyers.

"In particular, the complaint charges that the defendants failed to disclose a contemplated transaction with one of the center's largest tenants, the National Broadcasting Co, that would provide (it) with approximately $440 million in new, up-front capital," the lawyers said.
About a month after stockholders voted to approve the buyout, the deal with General Electric Co's NBC was disclosed.
The lawsuit was filed in U.S. District Court for the Distric of Delaware by individuals who held shares in Rockefeller Center as of February 8.
